text: In LiteRT 362759838, TriggerAcceleratorAutomaticRegistration registers accelerators in the fixed order NPU, WebNN, GPU, CPU, and when kLiteRtEnvOptionTagAutoRegisterAccelerators is not set the default set is CPU | GPU | NPU | WebNN.

LiteRtCompiledModelT::Create (LiteRT 362759838) iterates the environment's accelerator registry in registration order and applies each accelerator's delegate in that order, so with default auto-registration the GPU accelerator's delegate is applied to the graph before the CPU (XNNPACK) accelerator's.

LiteRT's RegisterGpuAccelerator (gpu_registry.cc) tries, in order: an accelerator definition passed through kLiteRtEnvOptionTagSystemGpuAcceleratorHandle, then the statically linked LiteRtStaticLinkedAcceleratorGpuDef, then dlopen of a platform-specific list of library names under kLiteRtEnvOptionTagRuntimeLibraryDir (looking up LiteRtAcceleratorImpl, then LiteRtRegisterGpuAccelerator); on iOS with Metal support the names include libLiteRtGpuAccelerator.dylib, libLiteRtMetalAccelerator.dylib and LiteRtMetalAccelerator.

LiteRT's litert_accelerator_library Bazel macro builds the static-link target (e.g. //litert/runtime/accelerators/gpu:ml_drift_metal_accelerator) with defines = ["LITERT_USE_STATIC_LINKED_GPU_ACCELERATOR"] and alwayslink = 1, and with that define ml_drift_metal_accelerator.cc contains a global StaticGpuAcceleratorInitializer whose constructor sets LiteRtStaticLinkedAcceleratorGpuDef = &LiteRtAcceleratorImpl.

In our LiteRT-LM fork (agello-next 7b872544, commit 43f0f5c3), //runtime/executor:default_static_gpu_accelerator depends (unless litert_runtime_link_mode=dynamic) on apple_static_gpu_accelerator, which selects @litert//litert/runtime/accelerators/gpu:ml_drift_metal_accelerator and links -framework Metal and -framework Foundation on both @platforms//os:ios and @platforms//os:macos; in upstream LiteRT-LM at df6df5b8 the default branch of default_static_gpu_accelerator has an empty dependency list.

In the recorded E4B engine run on an Apple M6 Mac (agello-bench, our build), the engine log shows NPU registration failing with kLiteRtStatusErrorNotFound, then the accelerator named "GPU Metal" registered with the message "Statically linked GPU accelerator registered.", then "CpuAccelerator" with "XNNPACK CPU accelerator registered."

sources.detail: Engine log: npu_registry.cc:34, accelerator_registry.cc:54 GPU Metal, gpu_registry.cc:116, accelerator_registry.cc:54 CpuAccelerator, cpu_registry.cc:73

text: LiteRT's Metal accelerator definition (ml_drift_metal_accelerator.cc) reports the name "GPU Metal", hardware support kLiteRtHwAcceleratorGpu, returns true for delegate-responsible-for-JIT, and registers buffer handlers (LiteRtCreateMetalMemory, LiteRtLockMetalMemory, ...) for exactly five buffer types: MetalBuffer, MetalBufferFp16, MetalTexture, MetalTextureFp16, MetalBufferPacked, with device tag kLiteRtEnvOptionTagMetalDevice and queue tag kLiteRtEnvOptionTagMetalCommandQueue.

LiteRT-LM's CreateEnvironment (runtime/util/litert_util.cc, agello-next 7b872544) creates the LiteRT Environment with only these options: magic-number configs and verifications (CPU, GPU, or generic NPU backend, unless configure_magic_numbers is off), NPU dispatch and compiler-plugin library directories (NPU backends only), and the minimum log severity when one is set; it passes no Metal device or command queue.

On Apple, the LiteRT GpuEnvironment is created by the ML Drift Metal delegate (delegate_metal.mm): it creates or reuses a process-global ml_drift MetalDevice, creates a new MTLCommandQueue with newCommandQueue, and calls runtime_context->gpu_environment_create with kLiteRtEnvOptionTagMetalDevice, kLiteRtEnvOptionTagMetalCommandQueue and the GPU-environment destroy callback and user data; GpuEnvironment then wraps the provided device and queue (LiteRtCreateWithCommandQueue) instead of creating its own.

In LiteRT 362759838, GpuEnvironment::Initialize logs "Failed to create OpenCL context." at INFO level whenever LITERT_HAS_OPENCL_SUPPORT is 0, which is the default on __APPLE__ builds, so the message appears on every Apple GPU environment and does not indicate a failure; the recorded Mac engine run shows it followed by "Created Metal device from provided device id".

sources.detail: Engine log: gpu_environment.cc:441 Failed to create OpenCL context., gpu_environment.cc:403 Created Metal device from provided device id

text: LiteRT-LM (agello-next 7b872544) enables file-backed (file descriptor) LiteRT model loading only for an NPU backend whose advanced settings turn configure_magic_numbers off, with the comment that magic-number replacement mutates the model flatbuffer in place; otherwise ModelResourcesLitertLm::GetTFLiteModel creates the litert::Model with Model::CreateFromBuffer over the section bytes from its loader.

LiteRT's ReplaceMagicNumbersIfAny (magic_number_utils.cc), for each signature matching a config's signature_prefix (null or empty matches all), replaces any value that is an exact multiple k*magic_number with k*target_number in tensor dimensions (also mutating the flatbuffer shape), in the parameter input of FILL (input 0), RESHAPE, BROADCAST_TO and RANGE (input 1) and SLICE (input 2), recursively in StableHLO composite decomposition subgraphs, and in integer attributes of odml.cache_update composites.

In the recorded E4B engine run (e4b-ours model, 8K window, our build on an Apple M6 Mac), LiteRT logged one magic-number config (magic_number=32003, target_number=8192, signature_prefix=null) and updated 577 tensors in signature decode, 426 in prefill_1024, 581 in verify, and 57 in mtp_drafter.

sources.detail: Engine log: magic_number_utils.cc:120 config[0]; magic_number_utils.cc:536 lines for decode, prefill_1024, verify, mtp_drafter

text: LiteRT's LiteRtCreateCompiledModel holds a function-static absl::Mutex for the whole call to LiteRtCompiledModelT::Create, so compiled-model creation is serialized across the process; LiteRtCreateEnvironment likewise holds its own static mutex.

In LiteRtCompiledModelT::Create (LiteRT 362759838), if kLiteRtHwAcceleratorCpu is not in the requested hardware set and any node remains undelegated after all accelerators are applied, creation fails with kLiteRtStatusErrorCompilation "Some ops are not accelerated. Add kLiteRtHwAcceleratorCpu ..."; there is no automatic CPU fallback for such nodes.

LiteRT-LM's CreateCompilationOptions (llm_executor_settings_utils.cc, agello-next 7b872544) sets the hardware accelerators of the GPU-backend LLM compiled model to HwAccelerators::kGpu alone and sets the fully-delegated-to-single-delegate hint, so with LiteRT's rule that leftover nodes fail creation when the CPU is not requested, any op the GPU delegate does not take makes the main graph's compilation fail.

Our LiteRT fork (commit 5083cfae) adds Agello telemetry to LiteRtCompiledModelT::Create: counters for compiled models, total nodes, GPU-delegated nodes, CPU-delegate nodes, undelegated nodes and GPU partitions, and a partial_delegation warning when the GPU is requested and either no node is GPU-delegated or some nodes are off the GPU or GPU partitions exceed the number of active subgraphs.

In the iPhone 17 Pro overnight probe run (build 2e54fbdb9ca9), probe06_digitConditions' telemetry recorded compiled_models 5, graph_nodes 19,983, graph_nodes_gpu 19,926, graph_nodes_cpu_delegate 3, graph_nodes_undelegated 54 and gpu_partitions 4.

sources.conditions: iPhone 17 Pro (A19 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, build 2e54fbdb9ca9 (LiteRT-LM 67d00f36, LiteRT 97e06d36), scenario probe06_digitConditions, GPU cases only, telemetry counters

formula: graph_nodes_cpu_delegate + graph_nodes_undelegated = 3 + 54 = 57; embedder ops + per_layer_embedder ops = 8 + 49 = 57

text: LiteRtCompiledModelT::RegisterBuffer (LiteRT 362759838): if the delegate registered buffer requirements for the tensor and the buffer's type is among them, the buffer is duplicated into the external buffer context and the tensor is marked kTfLiteNonCpu (no runtime copy), except that a host-memory buffer for a CPU-used tensor is also bound; otherwise host-compatible buffers are locked (read for inputs, write for outputs) and bound with SetCustomAllocation; failing all cases it returns "The given buffer type is not supported."

In LiteRtCompiledModelT::Run, when async execution is requested, async is set true afterwards only if at least one output buffer has an event attached; when it is not requested, Run waits with timeout -1 (no timeout) on every event attached to an output buffer before returning.

On LiteRT's Metal backend, GpuInferenceContextMetalLitert::GetPostDispatchEvent returns NotFound in async mode when it has no post-dispatch event, and DelegateKernelLiteRt::HandleOutputEvents then returns OK without attaching any event to the outputs (recording our async_unavailable telemetry anomaly); LiteRT-LM's decode always calls RunAsync, and the recorded E4B engine run reports gpu_async = unavailable: no post-dispatch event on the native and all simulated GPU families.

sources.detail: Facts lines: gpu_async = unavailable: no post-dispatch event (Apple M6 native and simulated A17 Pro, M2, M1); anomaly async_unavailable x1

text: At LiteRT 362759838, LiteRtCompiledModelT declares EnableCancellation() and Cancel() in compiled_model.h but compiled_model.cc defines neither (only SetCancellationFunction is defined); the C header litert_compiled_model.h tells users to use the callback or LiteRtEnableCompiledModelCancellation/LiteRtCancelCompiledModel, which are not declared or defined anywhere in the repository at that commit.

LiteRT's LiteRtTensorBufferType enum reserves values 30-39 for Metal and defines kLiteRtTensorBufferTypeMetalBuffer = 30, MetalBufferFp16 = 31, MetalTexture = 32, MetalTextureFp16 = 33, MetalBufferPacked = 34.
formula: Enum values read directly from litert_tensor_buffer_types.h

text: LITERT_HOST_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT is 64 bytes (documented as an immutable ABI constant), and LiteRT's managed host tensor buffers are allocated with posix_memalign at that alignment with XNN_EXTRA_BYTES of zeroed padding after the data; at XNNPACK d89ef666, XNN_EXTRA_BYTES is 16 except on Hexagon (128).
formula: Constants read from litert_tensor_buffer_types.h (64) and XNNPACK include/xnnpack.h (16, or 128 when XNN_ARCH_HEXAGON)

text: LiteRT's Metal buffer handler (buffer_handler_metal.mm) implements locking with a host shadow: LiteRtLockMetalMemory allocates a 64-byte-aligned host copy of packed_bytes on first lock and, for read locks, copies the GPU tensor into it (raw for MetalBufferPacked, a direct linear copy when possible, otherwise through ML Drift descriptor conversion); write locks skip the download, and LiteRtUnlockMetalMemory after a write copies the shadow back to the GPU tensor.

In LiteRT's litert_common.h, under defined(__APPLE__) the defaults are LITERT_HAS_METAL_SUPPORT_DEFAULT 1, LITERT_HAS_OPENCL_SUPPORT_DEFAULT 0 and LITERT_HAS_VULKAN_SUPPORT_DEFAULT 0, and LITERT_HAS_SYNC_FENCE_SUPPORT is 1 only for __linux__ or __ANDROID__.

Agello sets ExperimentalFlags.enableBenchmark = true when loading a model; the Swift Engine then calls litert_lm_engine_settings_enable_benchmark (creating benchmark params), EngineSettings sets AdvancedSettings.is_benchmark when benchmark params exist, and with is_benchmark LiteRT-LM sets the GPU sync wait type to kActive, in both the documented build and the shipped v0.18.0 sources; our passive-wait change (645aaf65) applies only when is_benchmark is false.

In the iOS arm64 slices compared in generated/binaries.md, the ML Drift Metal accelerator marker matches 12 defined symbols in Google's v0.18.0 CLiteRTLM and 9 in ours, with 0 string-only mentions in each.

sources.detail: Row 'ML Drift Metal accelerator (open since 2026-10-08) (defined / in strings)': 12 / 0 vs 9 / 0

text: LiteRtEnvironmentOptionsT::SetOption copies string option values into storage owned by the options object, stores non-string values (integers, pointers) as given, and without overwrite returns kLiteRtStatusErrorAlreadyExists for a tag that is already set.

LiteRtCreateEnvironment creates a GpuEnvironment only if the options contain one of twelve GPU tags (OpenCL device/platform/context/queue, EGL display/context, WebGPU device/queue/flush callback, Metal device/queue, Vulkan environment).

LiteRtEnvironmentT::SetGpuEnvironment fails with "GPU environment is already set." if one exists, and GpuEnvironment::AddEnvironmentOptions accepts only kLiteRtEnvOptionTagCallbackOnGpuEnvDestroy and kLiteRtEnvOptionTagCallbackUserDataOnGpuEnvDestroy, failing on any other tag.

RegisterAcceleratorFromDef rejects an accelerator definition whose ABI header is not compatible with version 1.0 or that lacks get_name, get_version, get_hardware_support, is_tflite_delegate_responsible_for_jit_compilation or create_delegate, then registers the accelerator and, for each supported buffer type, its buffer handlers in the environment's tensor buffer registry.

LiteRT's AcceleratorRegistry reserves capacity for 5 accelerators and 4 shared libraries and declares the shared-library vector before the accelerator vector so accelerators are destroyed before their libraries are unloaded.
LiteRtRegisterNpuAccelerator returns kLiteRtStatusErrorNotFound before creating an accelerator when no dispatch API is statically linked and kLiteRtEnvOptionTagDispatchLibraryDir is not set.

The Metal accelerator's CreateDelegate passes the options' weight loader to the ML Drift Metal delegate options (enabling constant tensor sharing when a weight loader exists) and, under __APPLE__, sets enable_metal_residency_set from the GPU options.

LiteRtCreateModelFromBuffer wraps the caller's memory in a non-owning tflite::MemoryAllocation after verifying the flatbuffer with a verifier max_size of SIZE_MAX (instead of flatbuffers' 2 GB default), and LiteRtCreateModelFromFd maps the byte range with a tflite::MMAPAllocation.

LiteRT-LM's POSIX MemoryMappedFile maps model files with PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE and MAP_PRIVATE (copy-on-write), and on __APPLE__ calls madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) on the mapping (MADV_WILLNEED elsewhere).

ReplaceMagicNumbersIfAny is called at the start of LiteRtCompiledModelT::InitializeModel only in builds without LITERT_NO_BUILTIN_OPS, and returns 0 without changes when the environment has no kLiteRtEnvOptionTagMagicNumberConfigs option.

LiteRT stores the magic-number configs option as a raw pointer whose strings must outlive model initialization, and LiteRT-LM's MagicNumberConfigsHelper keeps the configs and verifications in members it owns and passes their pointers as the kMagicNumberConfigs/kMagicNumberVerifications options.
LiteRtCompiledModelT::Create returns InvalidArgument when no compilation options are passed or the hardware accelerator set is kLiteRtHwAcceleratorNone.

When the GPU is in the hardware set, InitializeRuntime registers stub kernels for nine custom ops (Convolution2DTransposeBias, MaxPoolingWithArgmax2D, MaxUnpooling2D, moe, Resampler, custom_call.GroupNorm, custom_call.LayerNorm, custom_call.RmsNorm, custom_call.PixelShuffle); with only the CPU it stubs four.

InitializeRuntime always enables signature tensor names, and only when runtime options are present and parse does it enable StableHLO composite inlining and apply compress_quantization_zero_points, profiling, disable_delegate_clustering and the error reporter mode.

The C++ litert::Options::Build appends an opaque option payload only for option types obtained through GetOptions<T>() (option_slots_), so a compilation without a GetRuntimeOptions() call carries no runtime options; LiteRT-LM's CPU backend path calls GetRuntimeOptions() (compress zero points, delegate clustering).
InitializeRuntime sets the TFLite interpreter's thread count to the CPU options' xnn.num_threads when CPU options are present and the CPU is in the hardware set, and to 1 otherwise.
MarkSignatureIoTensorsNonCpu changes signature input and output tensors with arena allocation types to kTfLiteNonCpu so TFLite's arena allocates no host memory for them.
On non-Web platforms, LiteRtCompiledModelT::Create restores external weights into CPU tensors (as kTfLiteMmapRo) before applying delegates whenever the CPU is in the hardware set.

During delegate application, an accelerator responsible for JIT compilation is skipped when none of its hardware is requested, the NPU accelerator is skipped when the model has no dispatch ops, a null delegate from CreateDelegate is skipped, and a ModifyGraphWithDelegate failure returns kLiteRtStatusErrorRuntimeFailure "Failed to modify graph with delegate".

CheckCpuTensors records as CPU tensors all inputs and outputs of nodes that are not delegate nodes or that are TfLiteXNNPackDelegate or YNNPackDelegate nodes (excluding NPU dispatch ops); GetTensorBufferRequirements returns delegate-registered requirements for non-CPU tensors and a host-memory requirement of tensor->bytes otherwise.
Under __APPLE__, LiteRT-LM's GPU compilation options set PreferTextureWeights(false) and EnableMetalResidencySet from advanced_settings.gpu_enable_metal_residency_set.

Delegation metrics count nodes of active, non-delegation-skippable subgraphs; after each delegate, kTfLiteBuiltinDelegate nodes and dispatch ops count as partitions, the drop in other nodes is the accelerator's delegated node count, and non_cpu_fully_delegated_ is true only if no CPU-delegate nodes, no undelegated nodes and at least one node exist.

LiteRtCompiledModelT::Run fails if the number of input or output buffers differs from the signature's, or if any output buffer already has an event; inputs passed as nullptr get a zero-filled runtime-owned host buffer only when the tensor is used by CPU nodes and has no other backing.

RegisterBuffer resizes an input tensor to the buffer's shape when the shapes differ and the tensor's dims_signature has -1 in the differing positions; otherwise a mismatched input shape fails with "Input tensor shape mismatch".

Run calls AllocateTensors on the signature runner every time, relays scheduling info (default original uid = getuid(), highest priority), the async flag and per-run options to delegates through the external buffer context, maps kTfLiteCancelled to kLiteRtStatusCancelled and other Invoke failures to "Failed to invoke", and unlocks every buffer it locked through a cleanup.
LiteRtTensorBufferT starts with reference count 1, Duplicate increments it, and LiteRtDestroyTensorBuffer decrements it and deletes the buffer when it reaches zero.

LiteRtTensorBufferT::Lock fails with "Tensor buffer is already locked." if is_locked_ (a plain bool) is set, and if an event is attached and the buffer is not an AHWB it first waits on the event with timeout -1; Unlock fails if the buffer is not locked.

LiteRtTensorBufferT locks OpenCL, WebGPU, Metal and Vulkan buffers (and user types 100-199) through CustomBuffer, which looks up the handlers registered for the buffer type in the environment's TensorBufferRegistry; CustomBuffer::Alloc passes the environment option values named by the handlers' device and queue tags to create_func.
LiteRtCreateManagedTensorBufferFromRequirements creates the buffer with the first supported buffer type in the requirements, using their buffer size, alignment and strides.
TensorBufferRegistry::RegisterHandlers accepts re-registration of an identical handler set for a buffer type and returns kLiteRtStatusErrorAlreadyExists for a different set.

GpuBackendMetalLitert requests MetalTexture/MetalTextureFp16 for tensors with Texture2D storage and MetalBuffer/MetalBufferFp16 otherwise, with 16-byte strides, and MetalBufferPacked with no strides for non-external tensors.

CreateFromMetalMemory (LITERT_HAS_METAL_SUPPORT only) wraps an existing Metal buffer through CustomBuffer::Wrap, which requires the handler's import_func and does not take ownership; managed Metal buffers of all five Metal types are allocated with CustomBuffer::Alloc.

LiteRtEventType has SyncFenceFd = 1, OpenCl = 2, EglSyncFence = 3, EglNativeSyncFence = 4 and Custom = 5; custom events are compiled only when WebGPU or Metal support is on, and LiteRtEventT::Wait returns Unsupported for sync fences on platforms without LITERT_HAS_SYNC_FENCE_SUPPORT.
LiteRT-LM's LLM executor runs the decode signature with compiled_model_->RunAsync and async = true.

LiteRT compilation options identify their opaque payloads as "cpu_options", "gpu_options" and "runtime_options_string"; the CPU payload is TOML parsed into LiteRtCpuOptionsT, which embeds TfLiteXNNPackDelegateOptions and keeps the weight-cache path string alive.

LiteRT's C++ API calls the C API through RuntimeProxy, which uses a provided LiteRtRuntimeCApiStruct or, when none is given, GetLiteRtRuntimeBuiltin(); LiteRT's build defines link modes static (default), dynamic and none.

The C++ CompiledModel::Create overload taking a LiteRtModel does not take ownership of the model (model_owned = kNo), and the CompiledModel destructor destroys the compiled model before its members so the model stays alive while the runtime releases references into it.

LiteRT's in-repo cancellation guide states that LiteRT APIs are not inherently thread safe and that callers must handle synchronization; the C++ CompiledModel::Create documentation states that the environment must outlive the compiled model and any executions running on it.

In an Apple build of LiteRT 362759838, CreateManagedWithAlignment returns InvalidArgument for AHWB, ION, DMA-BUF, FastRPC, OpenGL buffer, managed GL texture and OpenCL types, and routes WebGPU, Metal and Vulkan types to CustomBuffer::Alloc, which needs handlers registered for that type.

In our LiteRT-LM fork, the --config=agello lines of .bazelrc set LITERT_LM_FST_CONSTRAINTS_DISABLED, C++20 for C++ and Objective-C++, -Wl,-undefined,error and the workspace status command; the static Metal accelerator comes from the BUILD dependency, not from a .bazelrc flag.

LiteRT-LM reads accelerator run metrics through LiteRtCompiledModelStartMetricsCollection and a metrics-collection helper for its executor statistics, and does not call the delegation-metrics API (LiteRtCompiledModelGetDelegationMetrics).

LiteRT-LM's EmbeddingLookupText::Initialize and EndOfMultiModalEmbedding::Initialize set the compiled model's hardware accelerators to NPU | CPU under __ANDROID__ and to CPU only on every other platform, so the text embedder, per-layer embedder and end-of-image/audio embeddings run on the CPU on iOS and macOS whatever the engine backend.

Agello's makeEngine passes Backend .gpu or .cpu() as the main backend and .cpu() as the vision backend and the audio backend (when enabled), and its engine attempts try the preferred backend with then without multimodal, then the CPU when the GPU was preferred.

LiteRT-LM's EmbeddingLookupText::LookupInternal performs one CompiledModel::Run per token (writing the token id to the input buffer and reading the output buffer), and LookupPrefill calls it once for each token of the prompt chunk.

In the recorded E4B engine run (2049 prompt tokens, our build, Apple M6), the embedding_lookups counter was 4098, which equals two embedding tables (text embedder and per-layer embedder) times 2049 prompt tokens.

sources.detail: Header: 2049 prompt tokens; Counters table: embedding_lookups 4098

text: The XNNPACK delegate's VisitNode switch (LiteRT 362759838 tflite/delegates/xnnpack/xnnpack_delegate.cc) has no case for EMBEDDING_LOOKUP, GREATER_EQUAL, LESS, LOGICAL_AND or SELECT_V2, so in E4B's embedder graph those ops run on TFLite builtin kernels.

sources.detail: Signature embedder ops: RESHAPE 2, GREATER_EQUAL 1, LESS 1, LOGICAL_AND 1, SELECT_V2 1, EMBEDDING_LOOKUP 1, MUL 1

text: For a CPU-backend LLM, LiteRT-LM's CreateCompilationOptions sets CPU options with num_threads = CpuConfig::number_of_threads (default 4), XNNPACK flags = default | TFLITE_XNNPACK_DELEGATE_FLAG_DYNAMIC_FULLY_CONNECTED | TFLITE_XNNPACK_DELEGATE_FLAG_ENABLE_LATEST_OPERATORS, YNNPACK from CpuConfig (default false), the XNNPACK weight cache file, runtime options compress_quantization_zero_points = true and disable_delegate_clustering from the advanced settings, and hardware accelerators = kCpu.

The Swift Engine (both the shipped wrapper 85b1a776 and agello-next 7b872544) passes only the backend string ("cpu") to litert_lm_engine_settings_create and never calls litert_lm_engine_settings_set_num_threads, so Backend.cpu(threadCount:) has no effect on the LLM engine, which keeps CpuConfig's default of 4 threads; only EmbeddingEngine forwards threadCount.

The XNNPACK delegate created by LiteRT's CpuAccelerator (TfLiteXNNPackDelegateCreate, no TFLite context) creates its own pthreadpool only when options.num_threads > 1; with 0 or 1 it runs on the calling thread, and TfLiteXNNPackDelegateOptionsDefault leaves num_threads at 0.

LiteRT-LM's ExecutorSettingsBase::GetWeightCacheFile names the XNNPACK cache <model path>_<mtime seconds>_<file size><suffix>, or <cache dir>/<model file name>_<mtime>_<size><suffix> when a cache directory is set, with suffixes ending in ".xnnpack_cache"; a cache directory of ":nocache" or a disabled weight cache returns an error (no cache), and when the computed file does not exist it first deletes files starting with the model's basename and ending with the suffix.

At XNNPACK d89ef666 (the version our LiteRT-LM WORKSPACE pins), kleidiai_enabled_by_default requires //build_config:aarch64 and :arm_i8mm_enabled, arm_i8mm_enabled_by_default matches //build_config:aarch64, and //build_config:aarch64 includes ios_arm64 and macos_arm64, so KleidiAI is enabled by default for Apple arm64 targets unless xnn_enable_kleidiai is set.

In the iOS arm64 slices compared in generated/binaries.md, the KleidiAI marker matches 638 defined symbols in Google's v0.18.0 CLiteRTLM and 637 in ours, and XNNPACK matches 6 defined symbols in each.

sources.detail: Rows 'KleidiAI (defined / in strings)': 638 / 0 vs 637 / 0; 'XNNPACK (defined / in strings)': 6 / 1 vs 6 / 1

text: At XNNPACK d89ef666, xnn_subgraph_rewrite_dequant_bmm rewrites a batch-matrix-multiply whose B input is the sole consumer of a qint8->fp32 convert into a convert(qint8 -> qcint8) feeding the matmul, leaving the channelwise scale array to be filled at reshape; reshape_convert_operator then allocates num_channels * sizeof(float) * batch_size bytes for the scales, where batch_size = xnn_shape_multiply_non_channel_dims (product of all dimensions but the last) when num_nonbatch_dims is 0.

sources.quote: Create new internal value: b in qcint8. Channelwise scale array is left null here; `convert(qint8 -> qcint8)` populates it at reshape.
const size_t bytes_needed = num_channels * sizeof(float) * (num_nonbatch_dims > 0 ? dq_batch_size : batch_size);

text: For a K-cache operand of shape [1, 2, T, D] read with transpose_b (channel dimension = T), unpatched XNNPACK d89ef666 sizes the convert's scale array at T * 4 * (1*2*T) bytes, 536,870,912 bytes (512 MiB) at T = 8,192, while the upstream fix (batch = product of all dimensions but the last two) sizes it at 8,192 * 4 * 2 = 65,536 bytes.
formula: unpatched: num_channels (T=8192) x 4 bytes x batch_size (1x2x8192=16384) = 536,870,912 B; patched: 8192 x 4 x (1x2) = 65,536 B

sources.quote: const size_t bytes_needed = num_channels * sizeof(float) * (num_nonbatch_dims > 0 ? dq_batch_size : batch_size);
const size_t channel_dim = transpose_b ? b_num_dims - 2 : b_num_dims - 1;

text: Our LiteRT-LM fork's WORKSPACE comment (agello-next 7b872544) records that without the XNNPACK patch the dequant-BMM rewrite costs Gemma 4 E4B 5.5 GB on the CPU for its INT8 KV caches; no raw measurement file for this figure exists in docs/agello/results/.

Upstream XNNPACK commit c72e2a4ae0efb7c648f73835e9a0133e7bf21a23, "Simplify batch size calculation for channelwise quantization in unary operators", authored 2026-09-22 19:37 -0700, sizes the qcint8 scale array as num_channels * xnn_shape_multiply_batch_dims(&input_value->shape, 2).

text: Our LiteRT-LM fork (commits 51f099fb, then b8f807ec) declares http_archive XNNPACK at d89ef6669a14db203b3b7935b1b3862cb63fb6df (sha256 aab0ed2b...) before tf_workspace2() with patches = ["//agello/patches:xnnpack_qs8_qc8_scales.patch"], a patch to src/subgraph/unary.c that computes qc8_batch_size = xnn_shape_multiply_batch_dims(&input_value->shape, 2) for the channelwise scale buffer.

text: LiteRT's CPU accelerator definition (xnnpack_accelerator.cc) has no buffer handlers, is named CpuAccelerator with hardware support kLiteRtHwAcceleratorCpu, is responsible for JIT compilation except under __EMSCRIPTEN__, and is exposed as LiteRtStaticLinkedAcceleratorXnnpackDef.

CpuAccelerator::CreateDelegate returns a null delegate when the CPU kernel mode is reference or builtin; otherwise it creates the XNNPACK delegate with the parsed options and sets kTfLiteDelegateFlagsHintFullyDelegatedToSingleDelegate when requested and YNNPACK is not enabled.

TFLite's EMBEDDING_LOOKUP kernel accepts INT8, UINT8, INT4 and INT2 tables with per-axis scales for float32 or float16 output, and its hybrid path reads only the looked-up row (col_size values at offset idx * col_size), unpacking INT2/INT4 and applying that row's scale.

Among the ops in the E4B file's TFLite graphs, XNNPACK's VisitNode has no case for CAST, SELECT, SELECT_V2, EQUAL, NOT_EQUAL, LESS, GREATER_EQUAL, LOGICAL_AND, LOGICAL_OR, LOGICAL_NOT, REDUCE_ALL, ONE_HOT, FLOOR_MOD, SIGN, TILE, UNPACK and EMBEDDING_LOOKUP, and has cases for FULLY_CONNECTED, BATCH_MATMUL, CONV_2D, DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D, DEQUANTIZE, QUANTIZE, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, SOFTMAX, GELU, LOGISTIC, TANH, RSQRT, SUM, REDUCE_MAX, SIN, COS, RESHAPE, TRANSPOSE, SLICE, CONCATENATION and PAD.

text: LiteRT-LM's EngineSettings::CreateDefault creates vision and audio executor settings with adapter_backend = Backend::CPU (comment: "Vision adapter can only run on CPU"), and engine creation logs a precision-loss warning when the vision adapter backend is not CPU.

LiteRT-LM's ValidateBackendConstraint fails engine creation with "<modality> backend constraint mismatch" when a section's backend_constraint list does not contain the executor's backend; the E4B file's tf_lite_audio_encoder_hw section has backend_constraint=cpu.

sources.detail: Sections table: 4 tf_lite_audio_encoder_hw backend_constraint=cpu; 5 tf_lite_audio_adapter backend_constraint=cpu; 8 tf_lite_vision_adapter backend_constraint=cpu

text: LiteRT-LM's vision executor sets CPU options with 4 threads for the vision encoder and adapter on the CPU, and the audio executor uses AudioExecutorSettings::GetNumThreads(), default 4.

LiteRT-LM's EngineSettings sets AdvancedSettings.disable_delegate_clustering = true for Gemma 4 models (llm_model_type has gemma4), which TFLite's interpreter option documents as disabling the reordering that minimizes switches between delegated and non-delegated nodes.

TFLITE_XNNPACK_DELEGATE_FLAG_DYNAMIC_FULLY_CONNECTED (0x8) enables XNNPACK for FULLY_CONNECTED with dynamic weights and TFLITE_XNNPACK_DELEGATE_FLAG_ENABLE_LATEST_OPERATORS (0x40) enables XNNPACK operators and features not yet on by default.

The XNNPACK weight cache file header (XNNPackCacheHeader) has kVersion = 4 and a stale flag, the reserved path ":memory" requests an in-memory cache, and the delegate loads or starts building a cache when a weight_cache_file_path or a file descriptor > 0 is given, logging an error and continuing without a cache if neither works.

LiteRT-LM's SetCpuCacheOptions passes a scoped cache file to XNNPACK as a duplicated file descriptor and a path as weight_cache_file_path, and logs that no cache is used when the cache file lookup fails.
LiteRT's cpu_registry target defines LITERT_HAS_YNNPACK only under litert_enable_ynnpack, and LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc sets --define=litert_enable_ynnpack=true only for build:linux_arm64.

The XNNPACK delegate logs "Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate for CPU." once per process (TFLITE_LOG_PROD_ONCE) when a delegate is created, and RegisterCpuAccelerator logs "XNNPACK CPU accelerator registered.".

LiteRT's CpuAccelerator creates each XNNPACK delegate with TfLiteXNNPackDelegateCreate (no TFLite context), so each CPU compiled model with num_threads > 1 gets its own pthreadpool rather than a shared one.

In LiteRT's litert_common.h: Android defaults AHWB, OpenGL, ION, DMA-BUF and FastRPC support to 1; Linux aarch64 defaults ION and FastRPC to 1 and AHWB, OpenGL, DMA-BUF to 0; other platforms default all five to 0; Apple defaults Metal 1, OpenCL 0, Vulkan 0; Windows defaults Metal 0, OpenCL 0, Vulkan 1; other non-Apple platforms default Metal 0, OpenCL 1, Vulkan 1; WebGPU defaults to 1 everywhere.

LiteRT's GPU registry dlopen candidate list starts with libLiteRtGpuAccelerator<ext>; on Android it then tries libLiteRtClGlAccelerator.so and libLiteRtOpenClAccelerator.so (with OpenCL support) and libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so (with WebGPU); on non-Android, non-iOS platforms it tries the WebGPU, then OpenCL, then Metal accelerators (each when supported); Vulkan comes last when supported.

LiteRT's generic GPU accelerator (ml_drift_gpu_accelerator.cc, name "LiteRT GPU"), in builds with WebGPU support, creates an ML Drift WebGPU delegate when the GPU options select WebGPU or when the backend is automatic and OpenCL is not supported, and an ML Drift OpenCL delegate otherwise.

In LiteRT-LM's prebuilt/ folder at df6df5b8, macos_arm64 contains libLiteRt.dylib, libLiteRtMetalAccelerator.dylib, libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.dylib, libwebgpu_dawn.dylib, libLiteRtTopKMetalSampler.dylib, libLiteRtTopKWebGpuSampler.dylib and libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib, while ios_arm64 contains libLiteRt.dylib, libLiteRtMetalAccelerator.dylib, libLiteRtTopKMetalSampler.dylib and libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib.

text: LiteRT registers its NPU accelerator only when a dispatch API is statically linked or kLiteRtEnvOptionTagDispatchLibraryDir is set; CompiledModel applies it only to models containing dispatch ops and, for not-yet-compiled models, first tries compiler plugins (with a compilation cache when kLiteRtEnvOptionTagCompilerCacheDir is set); LiteRT-LM sets the dispatch and compiler-plugin directories only for NPU backends.
LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc enables YNNPACK (--define=litert_enable_ynnpack=true) only in build:linux_arm64, and LiteRT's RegisterCpuAccelerator registers YNNPACK before XNNPACK when it is linked.

LiteRT's WebGPU accelerator reports the name "GPU WebGPU" and registers handlers for the seven WebGPU buffer types (20-26) with device and queue tags kLiteRtEnvOptionTagWebGpuDevice and kLiteRtEnvOptionTagWebGpuQueue.

Under __EMSCRIPTEN__, LiteRT's XNNPACK accelerator reports that it is not responsible for JIT compilation (so it is applied whatever the hardware set), WebNN registers only through the statically linked LiteRtRegisterStaticLinkedAcceleratorWebNn hook, and CompiledModel restores external weights for the CPU only when the CPU is the only requested accelerator.

On Android and on Linux aarch64, RegisterBuffer treats AHWB (when it has an AHardwareBuffer), FastRPC and DMA-BUF buffers as CPU-compatible and binds them by locking; sync-fence events, available on Linux and Android, are waited on by polling the fence file descriptor.
LiteRT-LM's text embedding lookup and end-of-multimodal embedding request NPU | CPU hardware on Android.
